content: Images and other media can only be used if they have been uploaded to WikiDoc. To upload images, you must use the designated upload page. Once uploaded, the images can be located in the image list. For guidance on image usage, refer to WikiDoc's image use policy. All information on this page is attributed to Wikipedia and its contributors. Detailed Instructions for Inserting Images and Syntax 1. Thumbnail or thumb: The image is scaled down to a standard width, which is user-specified and defaults to 180 pixels. A box is added around the image. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. By default, the image is placed on the right side of the page unless overridden by the Location attribute. 2. Frame: The original size of the image is preserved, and a box is added around it. If a caption is provided, it will appear below the image. 3. No specification: The original size of the image is preserved, and no border is added. If a caption is provided, it will not be displayed. 4. Border: Similar to the no specification option, but a border is added around the image. Image Placement (Location) Right: The image, including its box, is placed on the right side of the page. The text of the article flows around the image. Left: The image, including its box, is placed on the left side of the page. The text of the article flows around the image. Center: The image, including its box, is centered on the page. The text of the article is placed below the image. None: The image, including its box, is placed on the left side of the page. The text of the article is placed below the image. Image Size 100px: The image is scaled down to a width of 100 pixels. You can replace 100 with any desired number. If both thumbnail and a size value are specified, the size value takes precedence. If the image is already smaller than the specified size, it remains at its original size. 100x200px: The image is scaled to a maximum width of 100 pixels and a maximum height of 200 pixels. The original aspect ratio of the image is preserved. Captions Any element that cannot be identified as one of the above options is assumed to be caption text. Advanced Syntax for Inserting Images The new syntax is backward-compatible, meaning existing articles do not need to be changed. Several options can be set when including an image, affecting its placement, size, or presentation. These options include right, left, center, none, sizepx, thumbnail (thumb), frame, and alternate (caption) text. Options can be combined and separated by vertical bars (|). They can be placed in any order. Unknown options are treated as caption text, but this only applies if thumbnail is specified. If there are multiple unknown options, the last one takes precedence. An enlarge icon is also added to the lower margin of the thumbnail. Both the image and the icon link to the image description page, where the image is displayed in its actual size. The icon displays the link title Enlarge in its hover box, even if this term does not apply (e.g., when the image is already enlarged). Inline Rendering If none of the options other than sizepx and alternate (caption) text are specified, the embedded image is rendered inline. The none option can be used to create thumbnails without leftor right-alignment, which is particularly useful for tables. Additional Caption Formatting Options Additional formatting options for captions are available. All standard text formatting options apply. Inserting Multiple Images in a Gallery Format To create a gallery-like format, images can be displayed larger and centered. This is useful for presenting multiple images in a cohesive layout. Preventing Text from Floating Around an Image To ensure that text begins below an image and does not float around it, you can use specific markup. This is particularly useful for aesthetic reasons or when transitioning to a new topic. For legacy browsers, inline CSS may not suffice, but alternative methods, such as templates, can be used in certain namespaces. This version maintains the technical details while presenting the information in a clear, professional manner.
